page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The instance provides 40 physical cores with a single thread per core, backed by a 35 MB L3 cache. It features 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 4.8 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and utilizing a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.hfg6.10xlarge consistently within the average performance tier. The instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 38378.07 and a single-core score of 1438.99. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 2133.36 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 108.89 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In database operations, the server processed 34.78 million Redis SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 25.35 GB/sec. For small language model inference using a 135M parameter model, the system processed 1841.39 tokens per second for prompts and 76.66 tokens per second for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated core allocation and high clock speed provide stable, predictable compute resources without the overhead of hyperthreading. However, the absence of bundled local storage requires additional network storage provisioning, which may impact overall deployment costs and I/O latency. The instance is suited for workloads requiring high single-threaded performance and dedicated CPU execution, such as compilation tasks, web serving, database operations, and moderate multi-threaded decompression workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is an x86_64 server instance featuring a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with 40 physical cores, a 3.1 GHz clock speed, and 192.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks place this instance in the average tier, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 38378.07 and a Redis SET throughput of 34.78 million operations per second. The 1:4.8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated core architecture offer predictable compute performance for general-purpose and compute-intensive workloads. It is suited for database operations, software compilation, and web serving, though users must factor in the requirement for external network storage.
